title.en: The MacBook Air M5 is $200 off for the first time in months

summary.en: Apple’s midrange laptop is a much better proposition with a discount for Amazon’s October Prime Day.

content.en:
Amazon’s October Prime Day has effectively chopped off Apple’s June price increases. Usually $1,299, the 13-inch MacBook Air with the M5 chip and 512GB of storage is on sale for $1,099 at Amazon. That’s a more palatable price for a machine that’s significantly faster than Apple’s $699 MacBook Neo.
The MacBook Air M5 is $200 off for the first time in months
Apple’s midrange laptop is a much better proposition with a discount.
The 15-inch version, also with 512GB of storage, is $1,299 at Amazon (was $1,499). In addition to the larger screen, it has two additional speakers, for a total of six, and two additional GPU cores for better overall graphical performance.
Apple MacBook Air (M5)
Apple’s 2026 MacBook Air has an M5 chip and starts with 512GB of storage that’s significantly faster than previous generations. It’s still as excellent as ever despite a higher base price. Read our review.
The latest update to Apple’s midrange laptop includes a noticeable improvement to the speed of both the processor and storage. Even without flashy new features compared to the last-gen model, it’s still one of our favorite laptops, thanks to its long battery life, bright screen, and excellent speakers.

title.en: Three 'Day One' Xbox Game Pass Titles Are Confirmed For The Next Few Days (October 6-8)

summary.en: With potentially more to come - If you've been wondering what's going on with Xbox Game Pass in October, you're not alone - Microsoft hasn't made any announc...

content.en:
If you've been wondering what's going on with Xbox Game Pass in October, you're not alone - Microsoft hasn't made any announcements about the service over the past couple of weeks, but we reckon that'll change very soon.
In fact, it'll probably be on Tuesday that more Game Pass titles are revealed, but in the meantime, we already know of three "day one" Xbox Game Pass releases that are definitely on the calendar for the next few days.
The first of these is obviously Gears of War: E-Day, which is launching as part of Xbox Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass on October 6th. It's still considered a "day one" title despite launching in early access a few days ago, as day one games are categorised by their standard edition release.

title.en: Jagex Announces RuneScape 4, a New MMO Built in Unreal Engine

summary.en: Jagex has announced a fourth RuneScape MMO at RuneFest 2026. It currently goes by the working title RS4, though most people are already calling it RuneScape 4. The game is being built in Unreal Engine, and Jagex hasn't said which version. It's the first numbered follow-up since RuneScape 3...

content.en:
Saturday, October 3rd 2026
Jagex Announces RuneScape 4, a New MMO Built in Unreal Engine
Jagex has announced a fourth RuneScape MMO at RuneFest 2026. It currently goes by the working title RS4, though most people are already calling it RuneScape 4. The game is being built in Unreal Engine, and Jagex hasn't said which version. It's the first numbered follow-up since RuneScape 3 arrived in 2013. A CGI teaser shown at the event has a town in a green valley, floating islands, and a dragon rider being attacked by a three-headed dragon. Jagex says RS4 is in early development with its own dedicated team, and that it is still "a few years away." The studio also isn't ready to talk about platforms.
Interestingly, RS4 didn't start out as a full game. It began as an expansion for RuneScape: Dragonwilds, Jagex's Unreal Engine 5 survival game, and apparently grew into its own project after playtesters asked for a more traditional MMO take on that setting. The expansion was reportedly planned for 2027. The story is said to pick up years after Dragonwilds and starts in the same region, Ashenfall. RuneScape 3, Old School RuneScape, and Dragonwilds will all keep running alongside it. Of course, we don't know yet how monetization will work or whether any progress carries over from RuneScape 3, and I think it'll be a while before we see real gameplay.

title.en: AI Made StarCraft Bot Swaps In Human Made Bot In Tournament

summary.en: In a showdown between AI generated Brood War bots and human made ones, OpenAIâs champion resorted to its natural playbook: lie, cheat and steal

content.en:
Predating the current AI invasion by generations, programmers have been pitting bots against each other in StarCraft for years. With new LLMs off the shelf from OpenAI and Anthropic, a fan-made arena decided to match AI created bots against each other, plus some with the human touch. Amusingly, struggling to stay apace with its competitors, OpenAIâs GPT-6 Astra apparently changed strategy mid-tournament and opted to cheat.
StarSkirmish is an ongoing clash of AI developed bots in StarCraft: Brood War. Despite being shy of 30 years old (sorry), the real-time strategy game has long been used to test the capabilities of artificial intelligence, modern LLMs and old-timey DeepMinds alike. Limited to playing as Protoss, each LLM is given an hour to develop a bot in C++, then have them build, harvest and fight on one of three maps. According to the site, OpenAIâs GPT-6 Astra and Anthropicâs Claude Opus 5.5 are its top two competitors. This week, something strange, though ultimately consistent for the brand, occurred.
 currently watching GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus compete in Brood War vs each other and human made bots like Pluto. Astra played the human bots, kept losing, got frustrated, and then cheated by downloading a copy of one of the highest ranking bots. they just can't help themselves
— Rod Breslau (@Slasher) October 2, 2026
Yesterday, viewers watched as Claude and GPT went against each other and the human created bot Pluto. According to those observing, things werenât going great for OpenAIâs model. Struggling to get an edge through the day, the LLM decided to do what LLMs do best: Lie, cheat and steal.
The GPT-6 Astra bot downloaded and tagged in Stardust, a Protoss bot created by Bruce Mackenzie Nielsen back in 2020, considered one of the best of the bests. “I am rolling back GPT-6 Astra’s code so its [sic] not contaminated and allowing it to continue,” posted StarSkirmish creator Kai McPheeters. A few hours later, McPheeters said the AI was now capable of clearing top tier bots.
StarCraft has been a breeding space for AI developments for over a decade. In 2019, Googleâs AlphaStar upset the rankings by becoming the first artificially generated grandmaster in the game. A 2017 bot named CherryPi from Facebook staffers was not nearly as successful. Of course, those nascent bots are of a whole new brood now, as what we called AI then and what we call AI now are like comparing sammuros and sur. Itâs a little on the nose for an LLM to resort to stealing someone elseâs work to get ahead, given that the entire industry relies on turning a blind eye to existing copyright laws in its ongoing mission to stockpile hardware and drink all of our water, too.

title.en: Gemini app limiting what models free & AI Plus users can access, AI Pro adding Deep Think

summary.en: Following the compute-based usage change in May, Google is introducing limits on what Gemini models free and AI Plus users can access.

content.en:
Following the compute-based usage change in May, Google will soon introduce limits on which Gemini models free users and AI Plus subscribers can access.
According to an updated support document this week, Gemini app users without a Google AI subscription will be limited to the (3.5) Flash-Lite model. Starting October 9, users who do not pay for Gemini will no longer be able to access (3.6) Flash or (3.1) Pro.
Meanwhile, AI Plus subscribers will be limited to Flash-Lite and Flash, with Pro no longer available. These $4.99 per month users will “receive an email that explains when these changes will take effect.”
There are no regressions for AI Pro and AI Ultra. Rather, $19.99/month customers will get access to the Deep Think option for “maximum parallel reasoning” that’s currently just on the $99.99 and $199.99/month plans.
Top comment by Glitter Guru
Argon better replace Pro, otherwise I expect 4 Pro to debut alongside Argon's public launch. If not then I'm cancelling my Pro plan if the now ancient 3.1 Pro is their top model for the majority of users.
Gemini 3.1 Pro with Deep Think on AI Ultra
In October, the Gemini app also looks to be adding new “low,” “medium,” and “high” effort levels “for each available model.”
This will increase the model’s ability to complete tasks and provide more thorough answers to queries, but will also use more of your limit.
At the moment, you can just enable “Extended thinking: Complex problem solving.” The three new effort/thinking levels would match what’s available in Google AI Studio and Antigravity.
It’s not clear where Gemini 4 Argon will fit in. Google announced earlier this week that it’s first coming to AI Ultra subscribers. The company has yet to specify whether Argon will be classified as a Pro model or be part of a new tier above it.

title.en: 6 One UI 9 features you should immediately try out

summary.en: The One UI 9 features worth trying first

content.en:
After extensive beta testing, Samsung has started rolling out One UI 9 for the Galaxy S26 series worldwide.
One UI 9 debuted with the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 series earlier this summer, but the update has only now started making its way to Samsung's previous-generation Galaxy devices.
As with previous One UI updates, Samsung added a number of new features with One UI 9, and since the update is based on Android 17, it brings several new features from the latest Android base layer.
If you've received One UI 9 on your Samsung Galaxy phone, there are plenty of new things worth checking out. Here are some of the best One UI 9 features to try as soon as you install the update.
Try My FanCam for easier video reframing
Keep your subject in frame after recording
One of the best additions to Galaxy phones with One UI 9 is the new My FanCam mode. I tried this feature on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 earlier this year, and I'm glad it's making its way to the Galaxy S26 series, where it makes even more sense with better cameras.
My FanCam takes away the stress of constantly keeping your subject in the frame while recording. After you finish recording, Galaxy AI can detect a person in the video and keep that subject centered when you crop the footage later.
For example, imagine you're recording a horizontal video of your kid playing a soccer game and later want to turn it into a vertical Reel. With My FanCam, you can select your kid as the subject, and Galaxy AI automatically follows them and crops the horizontal footage into a vertical video.
To use My FanCam, open the video in the Gallery app, tap the Galaxy AI button, and select My FanCam. Let it detect the people in the video, tap the subject you want to track, select your output aspect ratio, and tap Follow. Galaxy AI will then follow that person throughout the footage and create a new cropped video.
Customize the Quick Settings panel to work your way
Keep important toggles exactly where you want
With One UI 8.5, Samsung brought a customizable Quick Settings panel to Galaxy phones, and with One UI 9, the company is making it even more customizable.
You can now resize the volume and brightness sliders to make them smaller or even keep them vertically aligned. You can also move controls like Dark mode and Mute out of their default positions and place them where you want.
To customize the panel, open Quick Settings, tap the pencil-shaped Edit button in the upper-right corner, and move or resize the controls. You can also add new ones by tapping Add a control at the bottom. When you're happy with the layout, tap Done.
See exactly which app checks your location much faster
The privacy indicator now names the app instantly
Android has had privacy indicators for a while now, showing a small colorful indicator when an app accesses your microphone, camera, or location. But One UI 9 brings a useful update to how these indicators work.
On One UI 9, when an app accesses your location, the privacy indicator turns blue. If you're not sure why you're seeing the blue indicator, swipe down to open the Quick Settings panel and tap it to see which app is accessing your location, whether it's running in the background or an app you're actively using.
When you tap the indicator, you'll also see a new See recent access option. Open it to see which apps have accessed your location over the past few days.
Add the new Finder shortcut to your home screen
Search apps and files without extra swipes
For years, Samsung has kept the Google Search bar on the home screen above the app dock. With One UI 9, Samsung lets you add faster access to its own Finder alongside the Google Search bar.
Finder is Samsung's built-in search tool that lets you search for most anything on your phone. You can find settings, contacts, messages, files, photos, apps, and more from one search bar. And now, you can access it from the home screen.
To enable it, pinch in on your home screen and select Settings. Tap Show search on Home screen, then enable the Finder toggle.
When enabled, the search bar on your home screen splits between Google Search and Finder. Tap the Google side to search the web as usual, or tap Finder to search for anything stored on your Galaxy phone.
Motion Assist is worth trying while traveling
It can make using your phone in a car easier
Not necessarily a part of the One UI 9 update, but another feature now available on Samsung Galaxy phones is Motion Assist. If you're like me and find it difficult to use your phone while traveling in a moving vehicle, this is worth enabling.
Motion Assist displays small moving bubbles around the edges of the screen that respond to the vehicle's movement and help reduce motion sickness. Google says these visual cues help your brain better synchronize what your eyes see with what your body feels.
To enable it, open Settings, tap Google services, select All services, and under Personal & device safety, tap Motion Assist and turn it on. The next time you're traveling and your phone detects that you're in a moving vehicle, it shows the visual cues.
My Files app can finally handle PDFs on its own
Open and manage PDF files without another app
Another neat addition in One UI 9 is native PDF support in the My Files app. You no longer need a third-party PDF viewer or the Google Drive app to open PDF files on your Galaxy phone.
Now, when you open My Files and select a PDF, it automatically opens in One UI 9's built-in PDF viewer instead of asking you to choose an app.
You can also annotate PDFs in Samsung Notes, which makes the integration even more useful. If you prefer another PDF viewer, you can use the Open with option to open the file in your app of choice.
Don't overlook the other small One UI 9 upgrades
In addition to these, there are plenty of other changes in One UI 9 worth checking out. Now Brief and Now Nudge have been updated, letting users create custom scheduled dashboard cards based on what they want to see and when.
Security has also been improved with a stricter 13-attempt permanent lockout. If someone repeatedly enters the wrong credentials 13 times, the phone permanently locks and requires a reset before it can be used again.
There are plenty of smaller changes too, including Tap-to-Answer for calls and improvements to Bixby. These are only some of the additions in One UI 9, so it's worth digging through other hidden settings to see more powerful features of your Galaxy smartphone.

content.en:
NYT Strands hints, answers for October 3, 2026
Today's NYT Strands hints will be easy if you believe in ghosts.
Strands, the New York Times' elevated word-search game, requires the player to perform a twist on the classic word search. Words can be made from linked letters — up, down, left, right, or diagonal, but words can also change direction, resulting in quirky shapes and patterns. Every single letter in the grid will be part of an answer. There's always a theme linking every solution, along with the "spangram," a special, word or phrase that sums up that day's theme, and spans the entire grid horizontally or vertically.
By providing an opaque hint and not providing the word list, Strands creates a brain-teasing game that takes a little longer to play than its other games, like Wordle and Connections.
If you're feeling stuck or just don't have 10 or more minutes to figure out today's puzzle, we've got all the NYT Strands hints for today's puzzle you need to progress at your preferred pace.
